paper_sections.title: Drift Diffusion Model and Domain Interaction
Parametric Representation of Stimulus Features Within the Brain
FPN Dynamics as a Function of Feature Salience

description.value: The study examined how perceptual salience and categorical salience, representing information at different levels of abstraction, interact during perceptual categorization and how these features are represented in frontoparietal brain networks.

design.value: Nine analyzed human participants performed a visual random-dot-motion categorization task during four fMRI sessions. Motion coherence and distance of motion direction from an oblique category boundary were independently varied, and behavioral choices, reaction times, diffusion-model parameters, and BOLD responses were analyzed.

source_definition.value: Perceptual salience was altered by changing dot-motion coherence: salience increased as motion coherence increased.

levels.value: 0%, 25%, 100%, and 1 intermediate coherence ranging from 12% to 15%

source_definition.value: Categorical salience was manipulated by varying the direction of motion of the dots: salience decreased as the coherently moving dots moved closer to the boundary line.
Mean accuracies in the 20 stimulus combinations were rank-ordered and placed into four separate bins.

description.value: Ten subjects participated; one subject was excluded because of a high percentage of aborted trials, leaving nine subjects for behavioral and imaging analyses.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal neural anatomy as assessed by a neurologist

exclusion_criteria.value: more than 20% of trials outside the response window within each run in two scanner sessions

task_description.value: Subjects viewed a variable proportion of coherently moving dots on a background of randomly moving dots and categorized the overall direction of motion as either leftward or rightward of an oblique category boundary.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to report their choice via a button press as quickly and accurately as possible, using the index or middle finger of their right hand.

stimuli.value: Random dot kinematograms with variable motion coherence, four coherence levels, and motion directions at nine distances from either side of an oblique category boundary inclined at either 45° or 135° from the horizontal.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner at the Henry H. Wheeler, Jr. Brain Imaging Center at the University of California, Berkeley; 12-channel phased-array coil

description.value: Functional images consisted of 32 slices acquired with a single-shot gradient echoplanar imaging protocol in a contiguous order.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner; 12-channel phased-array coil

description.value: Anatomical images consisted of 160 slices acquired with a T1-weighted MP-RAGE protocol.

Functional images were converted to four-dimensional NIfTI format, corrected for slice timing offsets, motion corrected, smoothed, coregistered to structural images, and normalized to the MNI_N27 standard volume.

steps.value: Converted functional images to four-dimensional NIfTI format
Motion correction with AFNI 3dvolreg, using the mean image of the first run as the reference volume
Smoothed images with a 5-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel
Coregistered functional and structural images with AFNI 3dAllineate using the local Pearson correlation cost function
Warped the anatomical image to functional image space using the inverse transformation
Normalized anatomical images with FSL fnirt to MNI_N27

model_settings.value: The model included A′ as decision threshold, x as stimulus salience, k as a proportionality constant linking stimulus salience to drift rate μ (μ=kx), and TR as mean residual time. Interaction, Distance, and Coherence model versions were compared using corrected Akaike information criterion.

estimator.value: An iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood of the diffusion model fit

hrf_model.value: gamma probability density function peaking at 6 s

model_settings.value: Separate regressors modeled the four coherence values and five unique distance values. Linear trends were tested using vectors transformed to zero mean with a sum of squares equal to 1. Only correct trials were evaluated for univariate analyses except the accuracy map.

level.value: first-level voxelwise fMRI analysis and group-level analyses

model_settings.value: Motion coherence and distance from boundary comprised the fixed factors and subjects the random factor.

interpretations.value: When processing categorical information, frontoparietal network areas exhibited a strong bilateral negative parametric effect.

interpretations.value: Perceptual information produced a predominantly positive parametric effect, with BOLD amplitude increasing with stimulus salience.

title.value: Parameter ranges across subjects for each model version

footer.value: Values are medians (interquartile ranges) for each model parameter (x, stimulus strength; k, sensitivity; A′, decision threshold; TR, nondecision time) for the 3 model versions, where lo and hi refer to lowest and highest stimulus salience levels. For the Interaction model, x (lo) and x (hi) refer to the lowest and highest levels of combined perceptual and categorical salience, respectively. For this model, a single value of k, A′, and TR was subsequently fit across all combinations of perceptual and categorical salience (see materials and methods). For the Distance model, x (lo) and x (hi) refer to the lowest and highest levels of categorical salience, respectively. For the other parameters in this model, lo indicates the lowest and hi indicates the highest level of perceptual salience. Conversely, for the Coherence model x (lo) and x (hi) refer to the lowest and highest levels of perceptual salience, respectively. For the other parameters in this model, lo indicates the lowest and hi indicates the highest level of categorical salience.

description.value: Parameter ranges across subjects for each diffusion model version.

footer.value: Values are median regression coefficients obtained by regressing model drift rates against motion coherence (perceptual), distance from category boundary (categorical), and their interaction with all 20 stimulus combinations included and with lowest-salience conditions in both domains excluded, with numbers of subjects (of 9) exhibiting significant regression coefficients in parentheses.

description.value: Regression coefficients for model drift rates and perceptual-categorical interactions.
